c. <u>Libraries</u>: No library is located within the Randolph Community. The Richmond Public Library operates a bookmobile service within the Randolph Community two days a week. The Randolph Community has taken the first and important step of setting aside renewal land in an area considered by the city's librarian as a preferred site. The actual construction of a branch library and staffing will be a decision of the city based on need and existing finances.
d. Fire Stations:
In Richmond two engine companies respond for every fire alarm, regardless of the nature of the fire, and additional companies are on call. Randolph is protected by two companies located outside the project area but within the recommended running distance as adopted by the American Insurance Company (A.I.A.) in their recommendations of January, 1963. According to these recommendations the distance from the fire station to the most distant area of coverage should not exceed two miles. The actual distance from either station to the most distant part of the Randolph Community is one and one half miles. On December 21, 1971, Acting Chief Barlow of the Richmond Fire Department in a meeting with a representative of Harland Bartholomew and Associates (consultant planners working with the Randolph Community) stated that "no one could disprove our service is adequate" and that "statistics would not justify a new fire station in the Randolph Project Area."
(2) After project completion the incident of fire will be reduced due to the elimination of blight and decaying wooden structures. The Redevelopment Plan will not adversely affect the existing fire protection service.
